discovery: Discovery of nuclear halos in neutron-rich drip-line nuclei

nominees.name: Isao Tanihata
nominees.affiliation: Research Center for Nuclear Physics, Osaka University, Japan / Beihang University, China

motivation: In 1985 Tanihata and co-workers used radioactive beams at Berkeley to measure interaction cross sections. They found that 11Li has an anomalously large matter radius. In 1987 Hansen and Jonson explained this as a neutron halo: weakly bound valence neutrons that tunnel far beyond the core. Jonson then led precision experiments at ISOLDE and GSI that confirmed the halo picture, including Borromean three-body structure and narrow momentum distributions. The halo overturned the textbook view of nuclei as compact drops with constant density. It opened the physics of the drip lines, established radioactive-beam facilities worldwide, and led to new theory, including few-body models and halo effective field theory. Today it is a demanding benchmark for ab initio predictions of how the strong force binds matter at its limits. The discovery is fundamental, and its consequences continue to shape nuclear physics four decades later.
